main_text.p: voluit. Hæc hæc Causa est potissima, cur Romanæ hierarchiæ Assertores Doctores Protestantes tam contemptim habeant; nimirum, quùm hi, si Papismo se addicere vellent, præsidere, præcedere, imperi-tare Regibus ad nutum Pontificis pof-sent; tamen propter Deum stulti facti,1.Cor.3.18. vt fiant sapientes, parere malint; nec Principes ludibria fieri, & quasi brutaLuther. animalia tractari patiantur.

Quid igitur? Non multi Nobiles &c.1.Cor.16. Te autem, (nobilissimorum religiosissime, & religiosorum nobilissime Princeps) Ecclesia Euangelica illius fidei religionisque DEFENSOREM expectat, quæ cœlestem coronam annuncians, terrenam etiam defendit. Et quia inter tribus ludæ & Leui maxima semper cognatio intercessit; hæc Tribus, quæ Dei, Regisque CAVSSAM ex animo propugnat, demississimè humilimé Clementiam Tuâ rogat, vt suos, tanquam Dei AngelosApoc.1.20.1.Thess.5.13. [illegible, ~18 letters], id est, in longè charissimorū loco habere pergat, idque

page.notes: Right margin: 1.Cor.3.18., Luther., 1.Cor.16., Apoc.1.20., 1.Thess.5.13. The Greek phrase after "Angelos" is not legible letter by letter, so it is marked illegible. The word "Doctores" is printed as a Gothic-looking form and read as Doctores with some doubt. The stray marks at the lower left and the show-through are not transcribed. No page number is printed.
